Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
Name: Accelerated Decay
Cardtype: Action
Clan: Samedi
+1 steath action.
Each Methuselah burns 1 pool, unless he or she burns the Edge.

Making it a  action against everyone is balanced by the fact Samedi has access to Obfuscate.
Burning the edge to avoid the effect force you to bleed as many times as you want to play the card, or take the pool damage as well.

Prince of Paris, France

Ratings Coordinator, Rules Director

Messages.Body: Samedi are in desperate need of new cards, but in terms of defence. Why would I play this, when I can just bleed for one? Compared to bleeding, this generates a lot of table hate (especially if you play multiple copies), and Samedi really want to avoid that.

Messages.Author: jamesatzephyr
Messages.Body:
> Von_Polack wrote:
> EDIT: Would it be overpowered if it did 2 pool damage, but only to your prey and predator, or you could choose who it targets (and targeted players get a right to block). I would play a multiacting Samedi deck featuring only these and Off Kilters.
>
4 pool damage against useful Methuselahs off one clan card is a fair amount of damage, even for a bloodline. Also, be careful how you word it, because that could be 4 pool damage in the end game, when your prey is your predator. Which is a fair amount. (Obviously, you could add something like "If there are more than two players in the game..." to the text.) Lily Prelude is perhaps the closest comparison I can think of - non-scarce Bloodlines clan, 4 unbounceable pool damage with an inferior discipline which is sort-of-the-same as being a clan card - but that requires passing a vote and costs a blood, though of course that can be against one Methuselah.

I was wondering if you could do something similarly inspired, but perhaps something like:

Accelerated Decay
Action, Some stealth, Maybe a cost
Do some pool damage to your prey. Additionally, if your prey has fewer than X pool (when this action is announced), you may also choose to do some pool damage to your prey's prey.

Which is similar to your "choose who it targets" version , but a bit more restricted. I was thinking along the lines of Foreshadowing Destruction. It feels a little more themey for infections, decay etc. too - the rot spreading from prey to grand-prey. "Some" might be 2 to your prey and 1 to your grand-prey, maybe? But whatever you fancy.

Messages.Author: jamesatzephyr
Messages.Body:
> Juggernaut1981 wrote:
> Accelerated Decay
> Action
> Samedi
> The chosen Methuselah burns X pool where X is 1 + 1 for each non-zombie ally and 1 for each vampire in their ash heap.
> (Some flavour text about dragging up the rotting dead)
>
The time is ripe for GreenO to re-create his (terrible) Yong Sun deck, now with added Samedi.

There are some potentially uncomfortable/annoying ways of getting crypt cards into people's ash heaps, which might be unpleasant to face. e.g. Might of the Camarilla. Not because such a deck would be significantly overpowered, but because it might start chasing the game down weird corner cases, where you're facing a deck that's doing unbounceable, high-stealth pool damage, so nixing the defences of bounce, moderate intercept, and reduction. And you don't have to be doing all that many weird things before the potential pool damage mounts up.

And it doesn't have to be that weird. Samedi have Obf/For, so something like Baltimore Purge + Renewed Vigor + stealth +... Vulnerability? Gregory Winter + Cloak/Veil? Maybe borrow Tye Cooper if you can find a Nec angle? Sacrificial Lamb is a bit poor. White Nights Massacre has potential - although the werewolf/extra copy angle, less so - especially given you would play it after the Baltimore Purge action has gone through. If feeling especially adventurous, the Harbingers have a couple of vampires with Obfuscate (particularly, Egottha and La Viuda Blanca) who you might borrow if you fancy some sort of Obf/For Purge deck, with added Crematorium.

And it's not that it feels Tier 1 Must Win the NAC in power, just that it feels a little bit 'out there' in terms of how other decks can interact with it. Potentially high stealth actions, that doesn't require bleed or vote or combat, meaning common deck styles might have extremely limited interaction potential with it.

Messages.Author: Juggernaut1981
brandonsantacruz
Messages.Body:
Your goals are good, but the means are terrible here. For one thing the wording doesn't make sense. Are you targeting non-zombie allies in the ash heap? Why does it matter if they are zombies? How many dudes do you plan on burning? How? Compress + amaranth? While the card is at least technically playable if the trick doesn't work, it is worse than a bleed for one because it doesn't get you the edge. True, you can target anyone, but Samedi are not known for their cross-table control, let alone winning. !Nos or FoS can lend some non-bleed ousting power much more effectively than this, so why use it?

If you want something else for Samedi to do, how about something that makes people pay pool to untap a minion? Why not an ability to burn blood to cause your prey to burn pool? How about a vote card?

Be careful when you fight the monsters, lest you become one.
